Added Sugars
+ To help identify sources of added sugars, look for ingredients that include the word
"sugar" or "syrup" or end in "-ose."
+ Added sugars may appear on ingredient labels under many different names, including
high-fructose corn syrup, agave syrup, corn syrup, rice syrup, fructose, glucose,
dextrose, sucrose, cane sugar, beet sugar, turbinado sugar, maltose, lactose, fruit
juice concentrate, honey, and molasses. Examples of non-nutritive sweeteners include
aspartame, sucralose, saccharin, xylitol, and acesulfame K.
+ Some foods and drinks, such as fruits and plain milk, have naturally occurring sugars.
The sugars in these foods are not considered added sugars.
